steps.title: Welcome to Procest
steps.body: Let's take a quick spin through case handling — we'll register a case together so you can see how the pieces fit. You'll add the record yourself.
Cases are the heart of your work. Open Cases from the menu to see everything in progress.
Register your first case — give it a title and pick a case type, then save. You can add tasks, decisions and documents later.
steps.task: Click New and save a case

steps.body: Your work lives here. Open My Work to see the tasks and cases assigned to you.
steps.task: Click My Work in the menu

steps.title: You're all set
steps.body: Nicely done — your first case is on the board. Head back to the Dashboard to track progress, and reopen this tour anytime from the … menu.

pages.title: My Work
pages._note: Case index scoped to the current user (assignee = current uid) in card view. A thin CnIndexPage wrapper because the stock index base-filter does not resolve the @me current-user token; the wrapper injects the resolved uid.

config._note: CASE archetype (unified zaak) — the flagship record and the ADR-062 reference page (the cell is the budget: every widget fills its gridHeight exactly, no inner scrollbars, no reserved voids). The lead row pairs the field-scoped 'Core case data' widget (include: identity/ownership fields) with a right column of KPI stats-block (open tasks / documents / decisions / sub-cases, replacing the deprecated header summaryAggregates) over the Related panel. Row two pairs the 'Process' data widget (include: status/procedure/workflow fields) with Initiator, Contacts and Notes sized to their small content. FK-scoped child collections (task.case, caseDocument.case, decision.case, voorstel.case, location.case) fit their rows to their cells with View-all/+N-more footers. Files and Calendar leaves close the page. lifecycleActions drive status transitions; audit history stays the single sidebar tab.

widgets.title: Initiator
widgets._note: Initiator (indiener) display — brp-kvk register sets. Resolved via page slots (widget-initiator -> InitiatorSection); self-fetches the case from the route id and renders nothing when no initiator is set.

pages.title: Sub-cases
pages._note: Bespoke parent-scoped sub-case (deelzaak) list: header carries a back-to-parent button, a parent breadcrumb link and a roll-up summary line, and rows deep-link into DeelzaakDetail under the same parent route. A standard list/index type can't express the parent-route binding (/cases/:id/deelzaken) plus the parent-context header and roll-up text.

pages.title: Sub-case
pages._note: Sub-case detail that shares the `case` schema with CaseDetail but adds a mandatory always-visible parent breadcrumb (parent → current) and a link out to the canonical CaseDetail edit view. The standard detail type renders a single object with no parent-context breadcrumb or cross-route hand-off, so the parent-aware framing requires a bespoke page.

config._note: OBJECTION-CASE archetype (AWB bezwaar), ADR-062 round 2. `bezwaar` is a supporting schema on a unified case (bezwaar.case) and declares NO comms linkedTypes — so NO files/notes/contacts/calendar leaves here; those live on the parent CaseDetail. The lead row pairs the field-scoped 'Objection' core widget (case/objection/status/awbReference/ontvangstdatum/decisionDeadline) with an in-grid KPI stats-block (advice-request and decision counts, replacing the deprecated header summaryAggregates). The AWB statutory-clock fields (verdaging/opschorting/hearing waiver/ingebrekestelling/dwangsom) are a genuinely distinct group and get their own 'Statutory clock & suspension' data widget. The two real child collections follow as FK-scoped object-lists side by side: committee advice requests (bacAdviceRequest.bezwaar) and decisions on the objection (bezwaarDecision.bezwaar), each deep-linking to its own detail page. lifecycleActions drive the bezwaar status (Ontvangen → … → Afgehandeld). Audit history stays a sidebar tab.

content.emptyText: No advice requests raised for this objection yet
No decisions recorded for this objection yet

config._note: DECISION-RECORD archetype (beslissing op bezwaar, AWB art. 7:11), ADR-062 round 2. No comms linkedTypes and no child schemas point at it. The 17-field schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Disposition & reasoning' (the legal substance — dispositionType, reasoning, legalBasis, advisoryOpinion, followsAdvice, deviationRationale, proceskostenvergoeding, status) paired with the Related panel (parent bezwaar and case), and 'Publication & documents' (the formal paper trail — replacementDecision, appealNotice, dates, decisionMaker, decisionDocument, publishedAt, notifiedRecipients) full-width below. lifecycleActions drive the status (draft → published). No files/notes leaves: document references are plain fields, not a files-leaf. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

CREATE-FORM archetype — the task creation form (route /tasks/new, usually pre-seeded with ?caseId=). A not-yet-persisted task has no id, so no children, history, aggregates or content leaves apply: it is just the Data form. No audit sidebar tab either — there is no object to have a history. All richness lives on TaskDetail once the task exists.

ACTION-ITEM archetype — a work item on a case (task.case) with assignee/dueDate/priority/status and an inline checklist[]. The schema declares NO comms linkedTypes and has NO child schemas pointing at it, so it stays deliberately lean: the Data widget carries the who/when/status and the checklist, and lifecycleActions drive the status machine (available → active → completed / terminated). No files/notes/contacts/calendar leaves — a task carries none of that content; those live on the parent case. Audit history (status transitions) is a sidebar tab.

pages.title: Case map
pages._note: Full-screen split view: a filter sidebar (case type + status) beside a CnMapWidget rendering RBAC-scoped case markers with clustering and auto-fit. Markers and overview are sourced from OpenRegister's maps-overview leaf (ADR-022, OR #154). No standard page type offers the sidebar-plus-map layout or the maps-overview declaration/points fetch lifecycle.

config._note: WORKFLOW-RECORD archetype (parafering/besluitvorming proposal). Intentionally kept as a bespoke full-page slot (VoorstelDetailView) rather than a widget grid: a voorstel is driven by its parafeerroute — currentStep, routeSnapshot (per-step actor/status) and the accord/return lifecycle need a live step-progress rail and inline accord/terugsturen actions that the generic data/object-list grid cannot express. The view renders the proposal document + bijlagen, the linked case and decision, and the routing timeline. The status lifecycle (concept → in_parafering → … → besloten) is driven inside the view. Audit history stays a sidebar tab; metadata remains available for provenance.

ADVICE-REQUEST archetype (adviesAanvraag on a case). No comms linkedTypes and no child schemas point at it, so it stays lean: the Data widget carries the request and its clock (case, adviseur, type, onderwerp, deadline, requestedAt, receivedAt, the questions[] and the returned adviesDocument), a Related panel exposes the parent case and adviser links, and lifecycleActions drive the status (aangevraagd → ontvangen / verlopen) — deadline-vs-received being the primary at-a-glance signal. No files/notes/contacts/calendar leaves: the advice document is a plain field and comms live on the parent case. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

pages.title: Workflow Board
pages._note: Bespoke Kanban board (one column per non-final status type, drag-to-transition) rendered by a host-app SFC; no standard page type offers the drag-between-status-columns workflow surface. Mounted directly (not wrapped in a dashboard widget) so its own header is the single page title.

config._note: CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype (WMS/WFS map-layer definition). Admin-only, no comms, no child schemas and no status lifecycle — so deliberately lean. The single Data widget holds the full endpoint config (url, layerName, srs, opacity, queryable, format, version, isDefault, active). No object-lists (nothing is a child of a layer), no content leaves (a layer carries no files/notes/calendar), no lifecycleActions (active is a plain boolean). Audit history (config edits) is a sidebar tab.

CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype (multi-tenant provisioning record — legacy, superseded by OR Organisation). Admin-only, no comms. The Data widget carries identity + contract + provisioning clock (slug, displayName, legalName, kvkNumber, contractRef, tier, isolationMode, dataResidency, createdAt, activatedAt, terminatedAt). The Provision + Refresh-usage admin actions are preserved as page actions, and lifecycleActions drive the status (onboarding → active → suspended → terminated). No object-lists or content leaves — a legacy provisioning record carries none. Audit history (provisioning events) is a sidebar tab.

CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype (initialling/approval route template consumed by voorstel records). No comms, no status lifecycle, no child schemas. The single Data widget carries the binding + defaults (name, caseType, voorstelType, isDefault, description) and the ordered steps[] (actor/actorType/mandatory/label per stage) — the routing definition. No object-lists, no content leaves, no lifecycleActions. Audit history (template edits) is a sidebar tab.

ORG-CONFIG archetype (partner organisation for cross-org case sharing), ADR-062 round 2. The schema is intentionally thin (name, slug, oin, contactEmail, defaultPermissionLevel, groupId, isActive, qualityScore/qualityStatus) — one coherent config group, no include-split. The lead row pairs the Data widget with an in-grid single-stat KPI card (share count, replacing the deprecated header summaryAggregates; deep-links to the CaseShares index). The one relationship that matters operationally — which cases are shared with this partner — is a full-width caseShare object-list (caseShare.partnerId=@objectId) showing label/type/permission/expiry; allowCreate:false because shares are minted by the share flow (token/password/audit), never hand-created from a list. No comms leaves (contactEmail is a plain field, not a mail-leaf) and no status lifecycle (isActive is a boolean). Audit history (activation/permission changes) is a sidebar tab.

content.emptyText: No cases shared with this partner yet

config._note: WORKFLOW-RECORD archetype (inter-organisation case handover). No comms/documents and no child schemas — a transfer is a small state machine, not a dossier. The single Data widget carries the request and its resolution (caseId, sourceOrganization, targetOrganization, reason, requestedDate, rejectionReason, completedAt), and lifecycleActions drive the status (pending → accepted / rejected). No object-lists (nothing is a child of a transfer), no content leaves. Audit history (the pending→accepted/rejected transition) is a sidebar tab.

CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype (workflow automation handler definition — a rule consumed by the workflow engine). No comms, no child schemas, no status enum (isPublished/active are booleans). The single Data widget carries identity + the handler-specific config[] payload (slug, type, title, description, tenantId, version, isPublished, active, config). No object-lists, no content leaves, no lifecycleActions. Audit history (publish/activation changes) is a sidebar tab.

pages.title: Public appointment
pages._note: Lib gap: anonymous/token-based public pages have no v2 typed primitive — see PublicCase _note for the same architectural reason. Collapse when nc-vue adds public-page support.

pages.title: Public status
pages._note: Citizen 'track your case' page. Resolves anonymously through OpenRegister's shares-leaf #[PublicPage] endpoint GET /apps/openregister/api/public/case-tokens/{token} (ADR-022) — RBAC-respecting, public-safe fields only. Lib gap: anonymous public pages still have no v2 typed primitive; collapse when nc-vue adds public-page support.

config._note: CASE-TYPE / WORKFLOW-DEFINITION archetype (the state machine that drives cases of a caseType), ADR-062 round 2. No comms. The schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Definition' (identity + versioning — title, description, caseType, version, lifecycleStatus, isActive, isDraft, parentWorkflow) and 'State machine' (the two defining graph payloads — steps[] with stages/roles/SLAs/checklists, transitions[] with from/to/guards/actions, plus editor nodePositions). Cases driven by this workflow are reached through their caseType index rather than a direct FK (case.workflowTemplate stores a version reference, not this object's id), so no object-list is scoped here. Publish/Deprecate/Clone admin actions are preserved as page actions and lifecycleActions drive the lifecycleStatus. Audit history (version changes) is a sidebar tab.

TRANSITION-RECORD archetype (an immutable entry for one case status transition). No comms/documents and it is itself a history entry, so it stays lean. The Data widget shows the transition and its side-effects (case, fromStatus→statusType, transitionLabel, noWorkflowTemplate, the evaluatedGuards[] that were checked and the dispatchedActions[] that fired); a Related panel links the parent case. No lifecycleActions — a status record is a frozen fact, not a mutable object. No content leaves. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

CONFIG/TECHNICAL archetype (Landelijke Handhavingsstrategie intervention matrix — versioned, immutable enforcement policy). Admin-only, no comms/documents. The Data widget carries header + axes + substance in one form (name, version, active, ernstAxis, gedragAxis, actorTypeAxis, createdAt, the cells[] grid ernst×gedrag×actorType→interventie, and the domain auditTrail[] of per-version actor/notes). lhsRecommendation records reference this matrix by version, not a FK, so no object-list is scoped here. No content leaves, no status lifecycle (active is a boolean). Register-level audit history is a sidebar tab.

ASSESSMENT-RECORD archetype (a per-case LHS intervention recommendation derived from an lhsMatrix), ADR-062 round 2. No comms/documents, no child schemas. The 13-field schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Recommendation' (the matrix inputs and outcome — case, inspection, ernst, gedrag, actorType, matrixVersion, recommendedInterventie, recommendedBy) paired with the Related panel (parent case and inspection), and 'Override & final' (the accountability-bearing deviation fields — finalIntervention, override, overrideJustification, overrideBy, overrideAuthority) full-width below. No status lifecycle field and no content leaves. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

GEO-RECORD archetype (a case location / BAG anchor). Deliberately lean: the Data widget shows address + coordinates + BAG identifiers (label, formattedAddress, latitude, longitude, nummeraanduidingId, parcelId, accuracyRadius, source) and a Related panel links the parent case. NO maps leaf here — the location schema does NOT declare a maps linkedType (only the case schema does; the interactive per-case map lives on CaseDetail and the /map overview). No comms/documents, no status lifecycle. Audit history (geocoding corrections) is a sidebar tab.

COMMITTEE archetype (bezwaaradviescommissie / BAC), ADR-062 round 2. No comms leaves on the schema. A committee is defined by its constitution and its caseload; the schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Committee' (name, type, domain, jurisdiction, quorum, active — the constitution) and 'Roster & term' (chair, secretary, members[], termStartsOn, termEndsOn, created — who sits and until when). The lead row pairs the constitution widget with an in-grid KPI stats-block (total assignments + in-deliberation workload via bacAdviceRequest.status, replacing the deprecated header summaryAggregates). Below: the roster widget full-width, then the advice-assignment object-list (bacAdviceRequest.commissie=@objectId). No status lifecycle (active is a boolean). Audit history (composition/term changes) is a sidebar tab.

content.emptyText: No advice requests assigned to this committee yet

config._note: ADVICE-ASSIGNMENT archetype (a committee advice request on a bezwaar), ADR-062 round 2. No comms leaves and no child schemas. The 15-field schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Assignment' (who/when — bezwaar, commissie, panel, status, assignedAt, deadline) paired with the Related panel (parent bezwaar and committee), and 'Advice & outcome' (the substantive opinion, dissent and evidence — advice, recommendation, conclusion, adviceIssuedAt, dissentingOpinions[], adviceDocuments, signatureEvidence, hearingReportRef) full-width below. lifecycleActions drive the status (assigned → in-deliberation → advice-issued / niet-ontvankelijk). Document references are plain fields, not a files-leaf. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

APPEAL-CASE archetype (AWB beroep at the rechtbank), ADR-062 round 2. `beroep` is a supporting schema on a unified case (beroep.case) and declares NO comms linkedTypes, so no files/notes/contacts/calendar here — those live on the parent CaseDetail. The 17-field schema splits into two genuinely distinct groups: 'Appeal' (the court header — case, sourceBezwaar, contestedDecision, courtReference, responsibleChamber, competentCourt) paired with the Related panel (parent case and source bezwaar), and 'Filing & judgment' (the clock, sub-process and outcome — appellantFilingDate/NotifiedDate, filingDeadline, voorzieningRequested, latefilingNotice, fileInspectionRequests[], judgmentOutcome/Date/Document, cascadeAction/cascadeBezwaarCase) full-width below. No status enum on this schema, so no lifecycleActions. Audit history is a sidebar tab.

pages.title: Termijn dashboard
pages._note: AWB termijnbewaking (statutory-deadline) monitor: a zaaktype filter drives a server-computed KPI bundle (total cases in period, within-term %, breached, at-risk) rendered as colour-coded compliance cards. The figures come from a dedicated deadline-aggregation endpoint, not a register query, so the standard dashboard/object-stats type can't supply or shape this data.

pages.title: Tenant onboarding
pages._note: Tenant onboarding wizard view: a per-tenant 7-step progress bar plus a go-live readiness check and an activate-tenant action, rendering TenantOnboardingService progress and validateGoLive() output. This is a stateful procedure/checklist surface driven by a service, not an object listing, so no standard page type can express the step progress and go-live gating.

pages.title: Substitution
pages._note: Self-service vervanging (substitution) page: an explanatory intro about scope/permissions, a register-substitution action opening the isolated SubstitutionFormModal, and a table of the current user's own active/past substitutions filtered to where they are the absentee (enforced server-side). The standard list type can't carry the explanatory framing or the self-scoped register/revoke flow.

pages.title: Substitutions & reassignment
pages._note: Coordinator substitution console: a filterable list of all substitutions plus register-on-behalf, revoke, inspect-capacity-stamped-actions, and bulk-reassignment actions (the latter two open dedicated modals). Coordinator role is enforced server-side. The standard list type cannot host the on-behalf-of register flow, the action-list inspection, or the bulk-reassign operation over the listed objects.

pages.title: Processing activities (AVG)
pages._note: FG/admin window on OpenRegister's processing-activity register scoped to procest (avg-verwerkingenlogging thin consumer): catalogue review status, unclassified-processing counter (OR-PA-4 fallback), and the per-betrokkene inzageverzoek export entry point (OR-PA-7 via InzageExportModal). All data comes from OR's /api/avg endpoints; OR denies non-FG/non-admin callers fail-closed (OR-PA-8). No standard list type applies — the data source is OR's AVG API, not a procest register schema.

observability._note: Declarative observability via OpenRegister's AppHost engine (ADR-040). Reproduces the output of the now-deleted hand-written HealthController + MetricsController. The /api/health and /api/metrics routes are aliased to AppHost\Controller\GenericHealth#index / GenericMetrics#index, so the engine reads this block at request time. Parity: metric names (with the engine-added procest_ prefix), types, HELP texts and label keys (incl. the caseType JSON field surfacing as the case_type label) match the pre-adoption contract; the implicit procest_info / procest_up gauges are emitted by the engine. The APCu controller-local cache is replaced by the engine's per-metric cacheTtl via the distributed cache (same 30s/60s TTLs, shared across workers).
